record.paper_title: Negative (and Positive) Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Identify an interesting property of a connected signed graph, analogous to the existence of an Eulerian tour in an unsigned graph, that corresponds to decomposability into negative circles or positive circles.

evidence.quote: Qn. 12±. Is there an interesting property of a connected signed graph, similar to existence of an Eulerian tour, related to decomposition into negative or positive circles? Ans. Unknown.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\Sigma = (G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a graph (loops and multiple edges allowed) and $\sigma\colon E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a signature on its edges. The sign of a circle (simple closed walk) $C$ in $\Sigma$ is the product $\sigma(C)=\prod_{e\in E(C)}\sigma(e)$; the circle is called positive if $\sigma(C)=+1$ and negative if $\sigma(C)=-1$. A decomposition of $\Sigma$ into circles is a partition of its edge set $E$ into the edge sets of circles. A classical theorem states that a connected graph admits a decomposition into circles if and only if it is Eulerian (every vertex has even degree), equivalently if and only if it admits a closed Eulerian tour.

Problem. Identify and prove a structural property $\mathcal P$ of connected signed graphs, analogous in spirit to the Eulerian property, that characterizes those connected signed graphs $\Sigma$ which admit a decomposition of $E$ into negative circles. Likewise, identify such a property characterizing connected signed graphs that admit a decomposition of $E$ into positive circles. The property should be intrinsic to the signed graph (not merely a restatement of the decomposition condition) and should reduce, in a meaningful way, to the standard Eulerian condition in appropriate special cases.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether there is an Euler-type property of a connected signed graph corresponding to decomposability into negative (or positive) circles is listed in the problem collection on negative and positive circles in signed graphs with answer "Unknown." Subsequent work has obtained partial results on related decomposition problems (e.g., balanced-cycle decompositions of 2-connected Eulerian almost balanced signed graphs), but no characterization analogous to the Eulerian theorem appears to have been established.
